Which original turbo elements are documented as retained?

RESEARCH RECORD [AUTHORED-007]:
TTE describes the 993 TTE650 5050 as an upgrade of the original K16/8 pair. It specifies a 50 mm compressor inlet with 6+6 blades and a 50 mm turbine outlet, retaining the original K16 turbine with blade clipping. These dimensions are supplier data, not complete manufacturing geometry.

The K16/8 hot housings and original K16 turbines are retained, with turbine clipping. The compressor and other components are modified; two wheel diameters do not define a reproducible design. [AUTHORED-007]

Can the 996 media archive validate this 993 upgrade?

RESEARCH RECORD [AUTHORED-008]:
TTE advertises 650 PS for its 993 TTE650. The consulted listing contains no complete engine configuration, measured 993 dyno curve, compressor map or turbine map. A linked media archive is named for a 996 product and cannot establish a 993 result.
No. A 996 archive is evidence for a different application unless exact compatibility and test configuration are established. The 650 PS figure remains a supplier capacity claim. [AUTHORED-008]

Can I send my original K16 pair for the TTE750 conversion?

RESEARCH RECORD [AUTHORED-009]:
The TTE750 conversion requires K24 turbochargers and explicitly excludes K16 donors. Its page specifies a 51 mm compressor inlet, a 54 mm turbine outlet and K24/10 hot housings.
The published TTE750 donor requirement excludes K16 cores. It requires K24 turbochargers; it is not the same upgrade path as the K16-based TTE650. [AUTHORED-009]

Is the TTE800 claim applicable to a stock K16 engine on unspecified fuel?

RESEARCH RECORD [AUTHORED-010]:
The TTE800 uses K24/10 hot housings and a replacement nine-blade turbine/shaft, with a 51 mm compressor inlet and 54 mm turbine outlet. Its more-than-800 PS claim is stated for 102 RON fuel and requires software changes. Maps and a complete operating envelope were not published.
No. It concerns a K24-based conversion and explicitly states 102 RON fuel and recalibration. It does not establish stock K16 capacity or durability. [AUTHORED-010]

What does the 250,000 rpm statement establish for this 993 turbo?

RESEARCH RECORD [AUTHORED-011]:
TTE describes VSR balancing equipment that can reach 250,000 rpm for some applications. This general process statement is not a 250,000 rpm continuous operating limit for the 993 TTE650.
It describes equipment or process capability, dependent on application. It does not establish the turbo operating speed or its certified maximum. [AUTHORED-011]

How should the RUF power be normalized?

RESEARCH RECORD [AUTHORED-017]:
The current RUF UK Turbo R page pairs 405 kW with 550 bhp at 5500 rpm and lists 700 Nm at 4800 rpm. The power units disagree: 405 kW is approximately 550.6 PS or 543.1 mechanical hp. Preserve the printed values and flag the inconsistency instead of silently changing the label.

Store the printed pair with a unit-conflict flag. A computed conversion of 405 kW is about 550.6 PS or 543.1 mechanical hp; it cannot justify relabeling the source as internally consistent. [AUTHORED-017]

Can the current rebuild specification be assigned to every original Turbo R?

RESEARCH RECORD [AUTHORED-018]:
RUF UK describes a current Turbo R rebuild with its own ignition and engine-management specification. Rstrada lists a historical Turbo R description at 490 hp and 479 lb-ft without the associated rpm on that page. These entries describe different source contexts and should not be merged into one original factory specification.
No. Keep current rebuild and historical descriptions separate. The available data do not establish that every original car used the current specification. [AUTHORED-018]

Does a related 3.6 litre air-cooled architecture establish stock K16 equivalence?

RESEARCH RECORD [AUTHORED-019]:
Rstrada describes 3.6 litre CTR2 and CTR2 Sport engines with different power and torque ratings and charge-air cooling arrangements from a stock 993 Turbo. It does not identify the complete turbo reference or publish compressor/turbine maps.
No. The engine configuration, intercoolers and turbo identity must be established separately. Related architecture alone cannot identify the stock 993 maps. [AUTHORED-019]
